title: Fifth dimension subgroups: D₅ = γ₅ when G/γ₂ is finite of exponent 3, candidates for a counterexample, and a reduction of Kourovka 20.84
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying S. Vorobev, "On the inclusion D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G): reductions, the Lie-ring proof, and evidence" (preprint, 2026; submitted to arXiv math.GR on 2026-10-22). The integral dimension subgroups D_n(G) = {g ∈ G : g − 1 ∈ Δ(G)^n} are defined from the augmentation ideal of Mathlib's integral group ring. Kourovka Problem 20.84 asks whether D_5(G) ⊆ γ_4(G) for every group; it is open and is not claimed here. Unconditional results: D_5(G) = γ_5(G) whenever G/γ_2(G) is finite of exponent 3, and more generally whenever G/γ_2(G) is a finite 3-group whose cubes form a cyclic group (paper, Theorems 6.6 and 6.8; the inclusion part of Tahara's 1981 description of D_5 is formalized for this); D_5(G) lies in the Jennings product M_5(G) for finite 2-groups of class at most 3; and, for "candidates" (the paper's minimal-counterexample shape among finite 2-groups of class 3), there is no candidate of order 2^11 with Q/P_3 ≅ Z/4 × (Z/2)^7 and none of order 2^11 and rank at least 8 (paper, Lemma 5.6 and Proposition 5.7). Conditional results, with every assumption an explicit hypothesis: the reduction of Problem 20.84 to finite 2-groups of class exactly 3 assuming D_3 = γ_3, Passi's D_4^2 ⊆ γ_4 and Gruenberg's residual theorem (Proposition 2.1); a minimal counterexample is a candidate assuming D_3 = γ_3 (Lemma 5.2); and D_5 = 1 for groups of order 2^11, class at most 3 and rank at least 8, assuming D_3 = γ_3 and the paper's computer result for order 2^10 (Proposition 5.7, D_5 form).
